headline: Where the Desert Drops Into the Sea
dek: Five coastlines that barely look real
editorial_intent: Deliver five vivid and authentic globally diverse examples of deserts or dry dune landscapes literally reaching saltwater, with precise site names for visitors to discover.
reader_scenario: A reader wants unusual sea landscapes and striking photographic trip inspiration beyond familiar blue-water beaches.
share_reason: This five-country carousel sparks the wait-where-is-that reaction with the rare sight of deserts falling directly into the sea, with photographs tied to real named destinations.
slide_count_rationale: Seven original licensed photographic scenes across six distinct coastal destinations, plus the scenic branded end card. One extra Namibia image deliberately contrasts two perspectives; the last location is a warm sunset dune walk in Maspalomas rather than a weak road-and-beach photo.
caption:
When giant dunes and desert cliffs meet the ocean, the scenery barely looks real. 🌊🏜️

📍 Sandwich Harbour, Namibia — huge desert dunes fall towards Atlantic surf; see them from two very different angles.
📍 Paracas, Peru — sheer ochre desert cliffs line the Pacific.
📍 Khor Al Adaid, Qatar — a remarkable tidal inland sea fringed by dunes.
📍 Dune du Pilat, France — climb a towering coastal dune above the Atlantic and pine forest.
📍 Cape Peron, Western Australia — rust-red sand borders Shark Bay's blue shallows.
📍 Maspalomas, Gran Canaria — walk a golden dune ridge with the Atlantic on the horizon.

Some are true deserts; others are enormous coastal dune systems. Which coastline surprised you most?

Photos: NIR HIMI, Kimberly Genest, World Thing, Dylan Shaw & Marco Canepa / Unsplash; Kevin Gong, “Sea meets sand dunes in Khawr Al Udayd”, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 (cropped and text added): https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/.
